children: National Stock Exchange of India on Thursday received clearance from the central bank to introduce futures contracts on corporate bond indices, paving the way for a new exchange-traded hedging and investment product in the fixed-income market.
The Reserve Bank of India's approval comes after the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) cleared the proposed contracts under the applicable regulatory framework, NSE said in a statement

Corporate bond index futures are designed to provide investors with a standardised and transparent tool to manage exposure to changes in corporate bond valuations, including movements driven by interest rates and credit spreads

Sriram Krishnan, NSE's chief business development officer, said the significant growth in India's corporate bond market had created opportunities for innovative products that cater to the evolving needs of investors
NSE said it would complete the necessary operational preparations before introducing the contracts
